decisions.reason: Despite its age, management is likely to continue this visibly launched software because it fits the firm's announced move toward data-driven infrastructure and past development effort invites justification rather than retreat.

Public commitment was weaker than for A, but it remains close to the core offer and can still be defended as part of the firm's connected infrastructure portfolio, so management would more likely persist than withdraw.

This product is less central to the firm's digital direction than the software and control products, yet its own-page launch and fit with the established infrastructure business make continued commitment slightly more likely than dropping it.
Control technology for water engineering machinery is highly complementary to the firm's core systems business, so sunk development effort and strategic fit strongly favor keeping it on the market.
As the newest product with a dedicated presentation and strong alignment with web-based, secure, data-driven operations, management would typically give it more time and retain it.
